statement: There are \(n \geq 3\) distinct positive real numbers. Show that there are at most \(n - 2\) different integer powers of three that can be written as the sum of three distinct elements from these \(n\) numbers.

\(ABCD\) is a fixed rhombus with an inscribed circle. Segment \(PQ\) is tangent to the inscribed circle of \(ABCD\), where \(P\) is on side \(AB\) and \(Q\) is on side \(AD\). Show that, as segment \(PQ\) varies, the area of \(\triangle CPQ\) remains constant.

A purse contains finitely many coins whose values are pairwise distinct positive integers. Is it possible to construct such a purse so that there are exactly \(2020\) different ways to select coins from the purse whose values sum to \(2020\)?

Let \(S = \{n^k \mid n, k \in \mathbb{Z},\, k \geq 2\}\) be the set of perfect integer powers. Arrange the elements of \(S\) in increasing order as \(a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \cdots\). Show that there are infinitely many \(n\) such that \(9999 \mid a_{n+1} - a_n\).
A simple graph \(G\) has \(19998\) vertices. For any induced subgraph \(\bar{G}\) of \(G\) on \(9999\) vertices, \(\bar{G}\) has at least \(9999\) edges. Find the minimum number of edges in \(G\).
